Synopsis:
Washington nonprofit Better Markets has filed a lawsuit against the Federal Reserve and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman, alleging that undisclosed private communications between Bowman and Wall Street banking executives corrupted the federal rulemaking process surrounding the Basel/GSIB capital rule overhaul. The suit claims these ex-parte interactions violated Administrative Procedure Act requirements and deprived Better Markets of due process under the Fifth Amendment. The contested capital rule, proposed in March, would reduce aggregate capital requirements for major banks by 4.8%. The rule is not yet finalized. The case represents rare litigation against the Fed and signals pushback from reform advocates against the Trump administration's regulatory rollback agenda.
